subject.title: feat: Force reply to originating channel (Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp)

question: Should OpenClaw automatically deliver final replies to a captured originating external route across internal/dashboard contexts, and should any fallback channel be allowed when the origin is missing or stale?
rationale: This is not just a mechanical routing bug: the chosen default can intentionally publish internal replies to external chats selected from stored or inferred state, so maintainer intent is needed before changing the boundary.

options.title: Define a sticky turn-origin invariant
options.body: Capture the inbound route at turn start and deliver ordinary final replies to that route unless an explicit policy suppresses or redirects delivery, with tests and live channel proof.

options.title: Add default-off force/fallback config
options.body: Expose explicit operator-controlled force-origin and fallback settings, but keep current defaults until route freshness, authorization, and failure semantics are documented.

options.title: Keep explicit delivery only
options.body: Leave internal WebChat/dashboard replies isolated from external routes unless callers set ExplicitDeliverRoute or use the message tool, and document that boundary.

recommendation.title: Define a sticky turn-origin invariant
recommendation.body: Capture the inbound route at turn start and deliver ordinary final replies to that route unless an explicit policy suppresses or redirects delivery, with tests and live channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The central reply-dispatch, outbound message policy, and security-boundary history most strongly route this decision to Peter Steinberger among the identified owners.
